title: Reversing embedded WebAssembly: part 2. Recovering function names from a WAMR .aot in pure C
content_md: ﷽ Hello, cybersecurity enthusiasts and white hackers! In part 1 we reversed the WAMR .aot container from real bytes and wrote unaot - a tiny, dependency-free C parser that verifies the \0aot magic, walks the section table (handling the 4-byte alignment rule), and decodes TARGET_INFO so we know exactly which CPU the embedded TEXT blob is compiled for. That told us where the native code is and how to disassemble it. But a disassembly of a few hundred anonymous functions is nearly useless. What a reverse engineer actually wants is names : which blob of machine code is add , which is fib , which is the exported entry point. This part builds exactly that - a symbolized function table - by decoding two more sections, EXPORT and FUNCTION , and joining them. We will also give the tool some color so the output is readable. Still one small C file, still no libraries. the plan The information we need is split across two sections, and neither one is enough on its own: FUNCTION gives us, for every defined function, the offset into TEXT where its native code starts (and its type index).
